statement: Let A_0 be nums. For t = 0,...,q-1, let A_{t+1} be the length-n array obtained from A_t by replacing coordinate p_t with x_t. For any length-n integer array a, let G(a) be the maximum of ∑_{i∈S} a[i] over all subsets S ⊆ {0,...,n-1} such that no i with 0 ≤ i < n-1 has both i∈S and i+1∈S; the empty subset is allowed. Then the function returns a result r and r = (∑_{t=0}^{q-1} G(A_{t+1})) mod 1000000007, where modulo denotes the least nonnegative remainder.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums) and q = len(queries). 1 ≤ n ≤ 50000, 1 ≤ q ≤ 50000. For every i with 0 ≤ i < n, -100000 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 100000. Each queries[t] has length 2; writing p_t = queries[t][0] and x_t = queries[t][1], we have 0 ≤ p_t < n and -100000 ≤ x_t ≤ 100000.

statement: If r is the result returned for (nums, queries) and r' is the result returned for (nums', queries), then r = r'.
preconditions: Let q = len(queries), let nums and nums' be two arrays with the same length n, where 1 ≤ n ≤ 50000 and 1 ≤ q ≤ 50000. Both inputs satisfy: all entries lie in [-100000,100000], each query has length 2, each query position is in [0,n), and each query value is in [-100000,100000]. Let p = queries[0][0]. Assume nums'[i] = nums[i] for every i with 0 ≤ i < n and i ≠ p; nums'[p] may differ from nums[p].

statement: Let A_0 = nums and A_{t+1} be A_t with coordinate p_t replaced by x_t for 0 ≤ t < q. Let B be A_q with coordinate p replaced by x. If r is the result for (nums, queries) and r' is the result for (nums, queries'), then r' = (r + G(B)) mod 1000000007, where G(B) is the maximum non-adjacent subsequence sum of B with the empty subset allowed.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums) and q = len(queries). 1 ≤ n ≤ 50000, 1 ≤ q ≤ 50000. For every i with 0 ≤ i < n, -100000 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 100000. Each queries[t] has length 2; writing p_t = queries[t][0] and x_t = queries[t][1], we have 0 ≤ p_t < n and -100000 ≤ x_t ≤ 100000. Let p be an integer with 0 ≤ p < n and let x be an integer with -100000 ≤ x ≤ 100000. Let queries' be queries with the additional final query [p,x].

statement: Let A_0 = nums and A_{t+1} be A_t with coordinate p_t replaced by x_t. For every t with 0 ≤ t < q, there exists a subset S_t ⊆ {0,...,n-1} with no i such that both i and i+1 are in S_t, satisfying: (1) G(A_{t+1}) = ∑_{i∈S_t} A_{t+1}[i], where G is the maximum non-adjacent subsequence sum with the empty subset allowed; and (2) for every subset S ⊆ {0,...,n-1} with no two consecutive indices, ∑_{i∈S} A_{t+1}[i] ≤ ∑_{i∈S_t} A_{t+1}[i]. If r is the returned result, then r ≡ ∑_{t=0}^{q-1} ∑_{i∈S_t} A_{t+1}[i] (mod 1000000007).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums) and q = len(queries). 1 ≤ n ≤ 50000, 1 ≤ q ≤ 50000. For every i with 0 ≤ i < n, -100000 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 100000. Each queries[t] has length 2; writing p_t = queries[t][0] and x_t = queries[t][1], we have 0 ≤ p_t < n and -100000 ≤ x_t ≤ 100000.

statement: Let A_0 = nums and A_{t+1} be A_t with coordinate p_t replaced by x_t. For every t with 0 ≤ t < q, the maximum non-adjacent subsequence sum G(A_{t+1}), with the empty subset allowed, satisfies 0 ≤ G(A_{t+1}) ≤ 2500000000. Consequently, the non-modular total T = ∑_{t=0}^{q-1} G(A_{t+1}) satisfies 0 ≤ T ≤ 125000000000000, and the returned value r is the least nonnegative residue of T modulo 1000000007.
